chart.reason: The dataset is fundamentally about ranking and distribution comparisons that read best as charts.

image.reason: Football evokes powerful editorial imagery — touchline, stadium, manager's chair — and the analytical density needs visual breathing room.

video.reason: No process or transformation; static-image atmosphere is enough and avoids generated-video uncanniness with footballers.

audio.reason: No meaningful sonic dimension to the dataset; audio would be decorative.

interactive_or_map.reason: A reader-quiz on the famous-name ranking maximises the surprise factor of finding Sarri above Pep and Ancelotti at the bottom.

des_teaser.label: Teaser hero image — manager dwarfed by empty stadium

content.prompt: A lone football manager in a dark coat stands on the touchline of a vast, empty floodlit stadium at night, viewed from far away through the dense fog. The manager is small in the frame, dwarfed by the empty stands and pitch. Cinematic editorial photography.

des_teaser.brief: Full-bleed cinematic image: lone manager dwarfed by an empty floodlit stadium. Dark, moody, muted palette. Sets the visual thesis — the man is small, the structure around him huge.
des_teaser.rationale: Echoes the core argument visually before any prose appears: the manager occupies a small fraction of the frame, just as he occupies a small fraction of the model's variance.

des_01.label: Hook chart — Messi vs Favre vs the rest

content.interaction: hover tooltip with role and exact value

des_01.brief: Horizontal bar chart comparing the impact of best-in-role figures on the same scale: top manager, top defender (p95 proxy), top attacker (Messi/Ronaldo), top goalkeeper. The Messi bar is roughly 2.46x the manager bar, visually dominating the row. All bars sorted descending by points_added.
des_01.rationale: The single most quotable comparison in the analysis. A horizontal bar makes the ratio instantly visible.

des_02.label: Forecast accuracy — error histogram

content.interaction: hover tooltip with count and percentage of team-seasons

des_02.brief: Bar chart of forecast absolute-error buckets across 1,470 team-seasons. The 0-5 and 5-10 bars dominate — visually demonstrating that the model is accurate enough to trust the residuals. The 30+ bucket is a thin sliver on the right.
des_02.rationale: Reinforces credibility before the punchier comparisons. Shows the model isn't a black box claiming impossible precision.

des_03.label: 12x — squad vs manager spread stat callout

content.label: Squad strength (80.8 pts) is roughly twelve times the manager-rating spread (6.56 pts)

des_03.brief: Massive 96px stat: '12×' with smaller dual-line label below. This is the structural fact the whole piece pivots on — display it as a headline.
des_03.rationale: The number is more striking as a headline than as a chart. Pair with a small chart for context.

des_04.label: Centrepiece — squad vs manager span comparison chart
des_04.brief: Two-bar chart: squad-strength spread (80.8) vs manager spread (6.56). The visual gap between the bars makes the 12x ratio register at a glance. Use the same x-axis for both bars so the manager bar looks tiny next to the squad bar.
des_04.rationale: Single decisive bar comparison. The picture IS the argument.

des_05.label: Famous-name ranking — interactive reveal

content.initial_state: Reader sees a question: 'Where do you think Carlo Ancelotti ranks among 596 currently-employed top-flight managers?' with three buttons: Top 10, Middle, Bottom 10.
content.transition: All three buttons reveal the truth: Bottom 10 is correct (-2.80, second-worst). The full famous-name ranking chart fades in below.
content.payoff: Reader sees Sarri above Pep, Klopp above Mourinho, and Ancelotti at the bottom — visceral proof the prestige order is not the data order.

des_05.brief: Guess-first interaction. Reader stakes a position on Ancelotti's ranking before seeing the data. After clicking, three buttons highlight (correct/incorrect), then a horizontal bar chart of all famous names (sorted by projected points) fades in below. Ancelotti's bar is highlighted in coral, others in slate.
des_05.rationale: The Ancelotti finding is the strongest emotional hook in the piece. A reveal interaction triples its impact compared to just plotting it.

des_06.label: Empty manager's chair — atmospheric image

content.prompt: Close-up cinematic photo of an empty manager's chair on a touchline, an abandoned wool overcoat draped across the back, against blurred stadium tunnel lights.

des_06.brief: Full-width image between sections — empty manager's chair with an abandoned coat. Visual metaphor for the sacking carousel: the chair is what we focus on, but it changes hands constantly without changing what's actually on the pitch.
des_06.rationale: Provides visual rest after the dense ranking section. Sets up the regression-to-the-mean section that follows.

des_07.label: Carryover decay chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip with carryover percentage and approximate seasons

des_07.brief: Line chart showing carryover percentage rising as games played increases. Annotate '1 season = 7.6%' near the left and '10 seasons = 45.2%' near the right. The slow approach to 50% is the visual proof that one or two seasons of data is barely a signal.
des_07.rationale: A line shows the decay relationship more naturally than bars; the asymptote-shape carries the meaning.

des_08.label: Stat callout — 45% repeat-overperformance

content.label: of overachieving managers do it again in their next job — barely better than a coin flip

des_08.brief: Big 72px stat callout with the 45% figure and the coin-flip framing.

des_09.label: Biggest single-season shocks — overperformers

content.interaction: hover tooltip with actual vs expected points

des_09.brief: Horizontal bars showing each top-10 overperforming team-season as 'TEAM YEAR' on Y axis, delta (points above expected) on X axis. Leicester 2016 highlighted in coral. Combine with the underperform list (ana_09) shown alongside in muted blue, mirrored to the left, like a butterfly chart — overperformers right, underperformers left.
des_09.rationale: Pairing the celebrated and disastrous seasons in one mirror chart drives home the noise-floor point: both extremes look like manager-stories but most are noise.

des_10.label: Tiny dial — closing image

content.prompt: Overhead minimalist editorial illustration of a tiny dial set on sprawling topographical terrain, conceptual style, muted palette.

des_10.brief: Conceptual editorial illustration of a small dial on a vast terrain — the literal visual metaphor of the closing argument.
des_10.rationale: Gives the closing essay a quiet image to land against.

des_11.label: Position-group player value distribution
des_11.brief: Grouped horizontal bars per position (attack, defence, goalkeeper) showing median, 95th percentile, and max points-added. Goalkeeper bar collapses near zero, attack stretches to 9.24. Visualises why squad spending priorities are the right lever.
des_11.rationale: Three-position grouping is more informative than a single ranking and reinforces ana_07's punchy 'goalkeepers move dial least' fact.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial — newsroom seriousness with a touch of stadium atmosphere
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: text-then-chart, with two atmospheric images breaking up dense analytical sections
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Avoid the typical scrollytelling-everything pattern. Use exactly one quiz interaction (the famous-name reveal) and let the rest of the page be a strong, restrained editorial chart sequence with breathing-room images. No video, no audio.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Stat callouts at 72-96px in a serif display weight; pull quotes in italic Georgia; subtle horizontal rules between sections; section titles in small-caps.
